findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed ice accumulation in front and back of kitchen walk-in freezer. Ice accumulation is not considered food-safe, and thus poses a cross-contamination hazard. Repair freezer as needed to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed dispensers used to dispense fountain drink and coffee cup lids to be soiled with food debris and soil accumulation. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed shelves in large display cooler used to store milk to be soiled with milk splash. Clean milk splash from shelving. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed tongs used at fryer to be stored handing off the fryer basket handle. Store in-use utensils in a clean food contact surface.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop head stored head down on floor in back area. Store wet mop heads in a fashion that promotes drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
Observed the only sanitizer dispenser for the facility to be malfunctioning in some way. The water comes out at 120F and the odor of sanitizer is very strong. Once the sanitizer cooled down to around 93, no sanitizer registered on the test strip. Sanitizer registers on a dark line at around 300ppm when the sanitizer is first drawn.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 
A box of clear plastic clam shell containers is observed on the floor in the kitchen. The sleeve of containers was removed from the box and placed in storage. Store single use items properly at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at the counter behind the soda fountian. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11. A fairly continuous drip is observed at the area where pizza dough is stored to temper and where pizza dough is measured into balls. The prep area for dough has been relocated until the leak in the store can be fixed.  The leak was called in before September 16th according to maintenance records becase records only go back that far and the leak and need to repair are not on the current record. Leak has been reoprted again.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11  (C) [Floors, Walls and Ceilings] in the area between the kitchen and hot holding counter are found to be in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily clean able.  Reference 6-201.11. The disrepair is causing a leak at an area over equipment. The leak has been on the repair list Since before September 16th according to maintenance. Please repair as soon as possible.
